target: Pecel lele biasanya dijual di tenda kaki lima waktu malam.
english: Pecel lele — fried catfish with sambal — is usually sold at roadside tents at night.
tip: Kaki lima = street vendors, named after the five-foot walkway (kaki lima) they occupy.

target: Sambal di warung itu pedasnya bukan main.
english: The sambal at that warung is unbelievably spicy.
tip: Bukan main = 'no joke', unbelievably: pedasnya bukan main = it is seriously spicy.

target: Tahu goreng ini garing di luar dan lembut di dalam.
english: This fried tofu is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.
tip: Garing and renyah both mean crispy: garing for fried-dry crunch, renyah for fresh crunch.

target: Telur setengah matang enak dimakan dengan roti bakar.
english: Soft-boiled eggs are tasty eaten with toast.
tip: Setengah matang = half-cooked: soft-boiled eggs, rare steak. Matang = cooked/ripe.

target: Di rumah kami, ikan lebih sering dikukus daripada digoreng.
english: At our house, fish is steamed more often than fried.
tip: Cooking talk loves di- passives: dikukus = steamed, digoreng = fried, direbus = boiled.

target: Ayah lebih suka ikan bakar, sedangkan saya suka ikan goreng.
english: Dad prefers grilled fish, while I like fried fish.
tip: Sedangkan contrasts two subjects: ayah suka A, sedangkan saya suka B = Dad likes A, while I like B.

target: Kalau masak untuk banyak orang, bumbunya harus ditambah sedikit demi sedikit.
english: When cooking for many people, the seasoning has to be added little by little.
tip: Sedikit demi sedikit = little by little; demi repeats units: satu demi satu = one by one.

target: Ayam kampung memang lebih mahal, tapi rasanya lebih gurih.
english: Free-range chicken really is more expensive, but it tastes richer.
tip: Ayam kampung is literally 'village chicken' – free-range birds that roam the kampung, pricier but lebih gurih. Ordinary farmed chicken is ayam negeri or broiler.

target: Sebelum dibakar, ayamnya diungkep dulu supaya bumbunya meresap.
english: Before being grilled, the chicken is simmered in spices first so the seasoning soaks in.
tip: Diungkep is a specific kitchen step: simmered slowly in the spice paste so bumbunya meresap. Direbus is just boiling in water – it wouldn't get the seasoning in.

target: Lontong dibuat dari beras yang dimasak di dalam daun pisang.
english: Lontong is made from rice cooked inside a banana leaf.
tip: English 'rice' splits in two: beras is the raw grain you buy, nasi is cooked rice on the plate. Lontong starts from beras, then cooks inside the banana leaf.

target: Akhir pekan depan kami mau membakar ikan di halaman belakang.
english: Next weekend we want to grill fish in the backyard.
tip: Grilling is bakar, never masak: membakar ikan = to grill fish. Masak = cooking in general.

target: Mas, nasi gorengnya pedasnya level berapa, ya?
english: Excuse me, what spice level is the fried rice?
tip: -nya makes a quality the topic: pedasnya level berapa? = how spicy is it (its spiciness, what level)?

target: Saya minta level dua saja, saya tidak kuat pedas.
english: I'll take level two please — I can't handle spice.
tip: Tidak kuat + noun = can't handle it: saya tidak kuat pedas = I can't take spice.

target: Teman saya kuat makan pedas, level lima pun masih kurang.
english: My friend can handle spicy food — even level five is not enough.
tip: Pun attaches after the word it stresses: level lima pun = even level five. Paired with masih kurang it builds the common 'even X still isn't enough' shape.

target: Minum es teh manis membantu kalau kamu kepedasan.
english: Drinking sweet iced tea helps when the spiciness is too much for you.
tip: Ke-...-an = overcome by: kepedasan = too spicy to handle, kepanasan = overheated.

target: Makan di sini atau dibungkus, Kak?
english: For here or to go, miss?
tip: The warung question: makan di sini atau dibungkus? = for here or to go? Bungkus = wrap up, take away.

target: Di warung Tegal, kamu tinggal tunjuk lauk yang kamu mau.
english: At a Tegal warung, you just point at the side dishes you want.
tip: Warteg (warung Tegal) = cheap point-and-choose rice stalls named after the town of Tegal.

target: Bayarnya nanti saja di kasir setelah selesai makan.
english: You pay later at the register, after you finish eating.
tip: Warung custom: you eat first and settle up after. Bayarnya nanti saja di kasir = just pay later at the register – no one expects payment before the food.

target: Tukang sate lewat depan rumah hampir setiap malam.
english: The satay seller passes in front of the house almost every night.
tip: Tukang + food = the seller: tukang sate = satay man, tukang bakso pushes his cart around.

target: Nasinya dicampur atau dipisah, Pak?
english: Would you like the rice mixed in or separate, sir?
tip: Soto question at the counter: dicampur (rice in the bowl) atau dipisah (rice on the side)?

target: Rendangnya tinggal dua potong, mau saya ambilkan dua-duanya?
english: There are only two pieces of rendang left — shall I get you both?
tip: -kan can mean doing it for someone: ambilkan = fetch (for you).

target: Bakwan jagung paling enak dimakan selagi masih panas.
english: Corn fritters are most delicious eaten while they are still hot.
tip: Selagi = while it lasts: selagi masih panas = while it is still hot.

target: Anak saya baru mau makan sayur kalau dicampur ke nasi goreng.
english: My child will only eat vegetables if they are mixed into fried rice.
tip: Baru here = only then: baru mau makan = will only eat (once the condition is met).

target: Suami saya yang masak setiap akhir pekan, saya bagian cuci piring.
english: My husband is the one who cooks every weekend; I'm on dish duty.
tip: Saya bagian X = X is my department: saya bagian cuci piring = I handle the dishes.

target: Resep soto ini turun-temurun dari nenek buyut kami.
english: This soto recipe has been handed down from our great-grandmother.
tip: Turun-temurun = handed down through the generations (turun = to descend).

target: Kalau malas masak, kami tinggal pesan makanan lewat aplikasi.
english: When we don't feel like cooking, we just order food through an app.
tip: Tinggal + verb = all that's left to do: tinggal pesan = just order.

target: Totalnya berapa, Bu? Sekalian sama es tehnya.
english: How much is the total, ma'am? Together with the iced tea.
tip: Sekalian = while we're at it, all together: sekalian sama es tehnya = including the iced tea.

target: Kita bagi dua saja, ya, biar gampang.
english: Let's just split it in two, okay, to keep things easy.
tip: Biar = casual supaya (so that): biar gampang = so it's easy.

target: Porsi bungkus nasi Padang biasanya lebih banyak daripada makan di tempat.
english: A takeaway portion of nasi Padang is usually bigger than eating in.
tip: Porsi bungkus = takeaway portion; Padang stalls famously give extra rice when you bungkus.

target: Durian itu baunya kuat, ada yang suka, ada yang tidak tahan.
english: Durian has a strong smell — some people love it, some can't stand it.
tip: Ada yang ... ada yang ... = some ... others ...: ada yang suka, ada yang tidak = some do, some don't.
